formation.explanation: Leader dispatch assigns term/index and persists locally, then self-matches and wakes per-peer replication. Replicators backtrack on mismatch, send bounded log batches or snapshots, and report successful progress into the tenure commitment object. Only eligible voter matches count; the majority boundary must reach the first index of this term. Main loop receives commit notification, updates configuration commitment, and queues entries. Followers accept matching predecessors, reconcile suffixes and use leader commit metadata to queue local history. FSM callbacks and futures complete asynchronously after queuing.

context.explanation: Follower contact timeout starts campaigns only with local voter eligibility; optional pre-vote precedes persisted term/vote advancement. Vote handling checks membership, known leader, term, prior vote and last-log freshness. Campaign-local replies form the authority majority. New leadership allocates fresh support state and a no-op. Higher terms, insufficient voter lease contact or removal cause loss; transfer catches a target up and sends TimeoutNow, temporarily suppressing new writes. Tenure exit detaches old support state and fails pending client/verification work.

connection.explanation: Log freshness and durable votes constrain authority acquisition. New tenure match accounting starts afresh, but retained log history may advance only when a current-term entry gains majority support. Latest configuration governs voter eligibility; stable-configuration admission waits for prior commitment and the tenure no-op, while truncation and snapshots reconstruct configuration context. Old replication replies retain the old commitment pointer, not the new tenure tracker. Already queued committed FSM work is separate from inflight work failed at step-down; leadership loss is an ambiguous client outcome. Startup reconstructs term, log/snapshot and membership before beginning follower work. Verification separately aggregates replication notifications; its numerical tally does not itself establish voting eligibility, which is the selected unresolved premise.

feedback.answered: The composed verification path has no observed suffrage filter: verifyLeader registers every replicator, notifyAll forwards booleans, and verifyFuture.vote only tallies. The separate lease checker does filter Voters, so timing and actual loss of authority remain essential premises. Current source also differs from the older membership proposal: AddVoter grants voting status directly and GetConfiguration returns latest, potentially uncommitted configuration. The map follows the current code and interface rather than treating the proposal as current behavior.
